chunks: And from him, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

"If Allah, Exalted and Glorious, said, 'Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world,' then indeed, the eight rak'at that the servant prays at the end of the night are the adornment of the Hereafter."

key_terms.آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ: At the end of the night
key_terms.زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا: Adornment of the life of this world

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of praying eight rak'at at night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) contrasts the Quranic description of wealth and children as the 'adornment of worldly life' with the eight-rak'ah night prayer, positioning it as the true adornment of the Hereafter. This comparison underscores the Shia emphasis on *Salat al-Layl* not merely as a ritual, but as the ultimate spiritual investment that transcends material prosperity, reflecting the tradition's focus on preparing for the eternal life through disciplined night worship.
